item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm not sure I fully understand how this qualifies as a skip

This is anomalous. No plants on Earth use carbon nanotubes (and biosynthesis of them is not a known process; current manufacturering requires lasers and a helium atmosphere), the vampiric feeding is totally unlike any other plant, and these are very likely an alien organism.

I don't think it counts either when you add in a 'nebulous 'another skip may have made it' or 'nobody knows where it came from' excuse.

There's no such requirements, SCPs don't need to have clear or unique origins. Many successful articles have unknown origins, or share origins with other objects, or have ambiguous origins.

item.content:encoded:
I agree with the "Atmospheric Mix" part. The rest of your critisisms I'm not all that on board with.

Buckyballs vs nanotubes is a goof, but a serious one? Don't buy it.

I think the vast difference between mahogony and grass is intentional. It's not grass, and this shows how the Foundation knows. I think it's a nice change from "unknown genetic makeup" or similar.

Heavy flame, I imagine, would be something like a flamethrower, as opposed to holding a butane cigarette lighter to it.

And saying that it looks like ordinary grass makes sense. There is no reason or need to be more specific. People know grass when they see it. Perhaps "common grass" would be better?

As for the ungulates… I don't care, I love it. :) Maybe they made hamburgers afterwards.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The good:
"Standard Atmospheric Mix #14"
- the very thought the Foundation has this nomenclature gives me a case of the warm fuzzies.

The Bad:
"A hollow core of cellulose and buckminsterfullerene". Fullerenes do a number of things, but this term specifically refers to a molecular structure similar to a geodesic ball - it's technobabble used in a completely incorrect manner.
-Given the age and rating, I'm hesitant to edit this myself, but it's a serious issue.
"SCP-355 is an unknown species indistinguishable to the naked eye from ordinary grass, but its nearest known genetic relation is the mahogany taxon"
-Another issue, with both Tone and Science. "Ordinary grass" is meaningless and highly dependent on region.
- "Mahogany Taxon"? This is also a possible problem. There are two major ways to classify living organisms.
:PhyloCode - I must admit, I don't know enough about it to speak to using this nomenclature under it. However, the existence of this entire form of nomenclature dates to early 2000, with version 5 being released currently/soon.
:Evolutionary Taxonomy - what you learned in science class. And under that system, "Mahogany" (Family Meliaceae) is as similar to "Grass" (Several Families in the Order Poales) as … a Salp (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salp) is to a Human Being. (They share a Phylum)
-TL;DR - Mahogany is not Grass.
I'd suggest just picking a photo with a known grass type, and saying it looks like that stuff. The current photo (I found an uncropped image that appears identical with Google) is unspecific - but appears that it MIGHT be Bermuda Grass.
"SCP-355 has been successfully destroyed by oxygen poisoning, heavy flame, anti-organic acids, and, in one instance, a variety of commandeered domestic ungulates. SCP-355 seems to be negligibly affected by poisons including [DATA EXPUNGED], in the form of tainted meat, vaporous herbicides, or soil toxification."
-Heavy Flame… as opposed to Light Flame? I prefer 1%, myself.
-Ungulates. hah. …still LOLFoundation. And this stuff would EAT Goats. It's Stabby, Acidic Razorgrass.

Sorry, neat idea, poor detail work. -1.

and, in one instance, a variety of commandeered domestic ungulates.

And there's upvote #50.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
For the same reasons as, for example, SCP-008. Or SCP-143. Or SCP-165. Or any number of other biologically-based SCPs.

And yes, it is an unknown species. It is phylogenetically distinct from any other known organism - there is no such thing, I assure you, as vampire tree grass, related to mahogany or not - and there are strong indications that it is non-indigenous to the planet ("deposited" is rather ambiguous - I have a fairly good idea of what SCP-CI-103 is, but did not replicate it in the entry, as in any other document).

item.content:encoded: My question is, why is this even an SCP? Even if it kills stuff, it does so in a purely physical manner. It's a plant. It evolved that way. It warrants containment because it could damage an ecosystem if released, but that's not 'Special' containment. Also, it's not an unknown species if we know what its genes look like. Just make up some binomial nomenclature.
